headline: Readiness is low again (33.6, HRV-driven) — today's easy run stays easy, full stop.
body_state: HRV 36ms last night — below your normal band, and the deterministic verdict is red: postpone quality, easy running only. Sleep score 70 on 7.9h, but 14-day sleep debt sits at 25h, so the tank isn't full even after a decent night. Training readiness 33.6/100 (Garmin: Recovery), body battery recovered +45 overnight to 46. TSB -17 (still inside the -5…-30 productive band) and overtraining status green — this is a recovery day, not a red-flag day, but the HRV/sleep signal is real and specific to today.
session: The plan already has today right: 7km Easy Run @ 4:51–5:20/km, no quality attached — exactly what the readiness verdict calls for. The catch is execution: your last three “easy” efforts (Aug 5, 10, 12) all ran 89%+ of the time in HR zone 3, 20–30 s/km faster than the band. Today, hold HR under ~130 (zone 1–2) even if that means the slow end of 5:00–5:20/km — slower than will feel natural. Cadence has sat 154–160 spm against a 168–172 target; a quick-feet cue (short, light steps) helps hit both the pace ceiling and the cadence target at once.
recent: Aug 12's tempo run told the real story: cut to 78% of planned volume (5.43 vs 7km), and even the tempo segment landed at 4:38/km with HR only 143 — 20bpm under your 163 threshold despite RPE 8. That's a fatigue flag, not a fitness one: the body pulled the plug on threshold work before you consciously chose to. Aug 13's Un1t class ran a similar zone-2/3 pattern (52% zone 3 of 41 min). Aug 11 stacked Un1t plus a 2h bike ride same day. Three straight days of moderate-intensity “easy” or maintenance work, no true recovery — that's exactly what today's readiness score is responding to.
focus: Hold today's easy run genuinely easy — HR under 130, even if pace slows to 5:00-5:20/km
Protect sleep: 25h of 14-day debt is the readiness driver, not training load
Next hard session (Aug 17 speed reps) waits for HRV back in range before it goes ahead
